summary: 4 working weeks, accrued monthly; the employer chooses the remedy when a public holiday falls on a day the employee does not work; leave interrupted by certified illness can be rescheduled.

owner.role: Employment counsel (IE) + HR Business Partner Dublin

locationAssumption.citation: Employees assumed to work in Ireland

rule.citation: OWTA 1997 s.19: annual leave measured in working weeks; public holidays are a separate entitlement (s.21)

source.citation: OWTA 1997 Second Schedule as amended (St Brigid's Day from 2023: first Monday in February, or 1 Feb if a Friday)

rule.citation: OWTA 1997 s.21: for a holiday the employee would not otherwise work, the employer chooses a paid day off within a month, an extra day of annual leave, or an extra day's pay. Part-timers qualify after 40 hours in the prior 5 weeks
rule.note: Choice of "extra day of annual leave" for Groupon is an assumption.

rule.citation: OWTA 1997 s.19(1)(a): 4 working weeks in a leave year with ≥1,365 hours worked
rule.note: Irregular-hours staff would use the 8%-of-hours method — not modelled.

rule.citation: OWTA 1997 s.19(1)(b): ⅓ of a working week per calendar month; certified sick days count as worked (s.19(1A), WRA 2015 s.86)
OWTA 1997 s.20(1)(c): leave may be taken within 6 months of the next year with the employee's consent
rule.note: Cap of 5 days is a Groupon policy assumption.

rule.citation: OWTA 1997 as amended by the Work Life Balance and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2023: certified illness during annual leave is treated as sick leave
rule.note: Exact section and commencement to verify.

rule.citation: OWTA 1997 s.23: compensation for untaken leave on cesser of employment

extras.label: Statutory sick pay
extras.citation: Sick Leave Act 2022: statutory sick days (separate from annual leave) — 5 days in 2026
